title: Asymmetric prefrontal representations for leader-follower dynamics.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Zenodo record 20723195 via its API: CC-BY-4.0, 5 files: ctable_light_combined.mat (784,781,359 bytes) plus imaging_data.zip/.z01-.z03 (~172 GB total). A ranged read of the first bytes of the .mat shows a 'MATLAB 7.3 MAT-file' (HDF5 container) created Jan 2026; the file was not downloaded (over the 50 MB cap). The GitHub repo HerbertWuLab/Yuan_manuscript_2026 was listed: MATLAB scripts show ctable is a MATLAB table with one row per session (columns pair, cp_rate, phase, cno, and a nested per-trial table 'stable'). I opened the one small data file in the repo, YC069_phase4a_correct_traj_nose_neck_rot.txt: 64,793 rows x 13 columns (frame number, nose/neck x-y for both mice, trial_no, trial_type 1-4, correct), 1,024 trials, no missing values, correct = 1 on every row (correct trials only), one pair only.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 89 pairs trained, 88 reached criterion; 673 sessions from 40 pairs in the role analyses; 30 fps tracking with SLEAP; calcium imaging in 6 leaders and 6 followers (82 sessions); the leader on a trial is defined from arrival order at the reward zone; per-trial counts across the whole cohort and the full set of columns in the nested trial tables were not verified.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo, CC-BY-4.0, no login; checked via the Zenodo API and a ranged read of the .mat file.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Per the MATLAB scripts (not opened), the nested per-trial tables hold leader, initiator, outcome and arrival times as columns; in the opened one-pair text file only trial_type (reward zone) and correct (all 1) are present.

a3_inputs_present.note: Trajectories are present as x-y coordinates (verified in the one-pair text file); no identifier lookups needed.

a4_units_stated.note: Paper states 30 fps; coordinates look like centimetres centred on the arena (values roughly -25 to 25), but no units are written in the file itself.

a5_enough_rows.note: Tens of thousands of trials likely (1,024 correct trials in one pair alone), but the independent unit is the pair: 40 pairs in the role analyses and only 12 imaged mice. Total trial count not verified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: Behaviour: 785 MB MATLAB v7.3 table; neural: ~172 GB split zip
a6_fits_laptop.note: The neural data, which is the paper's novel part, is ~172 GB of imaging archives (verified sizes) and cannot be subset without downloading it all; only the behavioural table fits, and it is a MATLAB table object that Python readers generally cannot decode without MATLAB.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable without opening the 785 MB .mat; the paper's internal counts (89 pairs, 40 pairs, 673 sessions) are self-consistent.

a8_label_provenance.note: The interesting behavioural label (who led a trial) is defined from which mouse reaches the reward zone first, i.e. computed from the same trajectories a model would use as input; the zone choice on correct trials is set by the moving visual cue, so it is near-trivial.

existing_models.name: The paper's own multi-agent inverse reinforcement learning (MAIRL) value-function model and logistic choice models
existing_models.score_and_split: Model comparison by nested chi-squared tests and log-likelihood gain per animal; 'self + distance' model beats baseline at predicting reward-zone choice; no held-out-pair evaluation reported.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved as a specific sentence; value encoding was weaker and less consistent in leader sessions than in followers.

existing_models.name: LISBET, a self-supervised transformer for social behaviour from body-tracking coordinates (used in this paper)
existing_models.score_and_split: Used here for unsupervised motif segmentation across 20 pairs; no predictive score for leader/follower reported.

existing_models.name: MABe / MABe22 multi-agent behaviour benchmarks (T-BERT, T-GPT, T-PointNet representation models)
existing_models.score_and_split: Frame-level behaviour classification and representation-learning tasks on other mouse dyad/triad datasets; not this task.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Methods from human action datasets do not fully transfer to animal data (from the search summary).

backbone.name: LISBET (pose-trajectory transformer) or CEBRA embeddings
backbone.hardware: CPU for behaviour embeddings; neural data unusable on a laptop

integration.join_key: none (no shared identifiers; only a shared data type)
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: No join exists; at most a transfer test of pose embeddings between arenas, which does not address the leader-follower question.

controls.positive_control: Reward zone on correct trials should be decodable from late-trial trajectory almost perfectly.
controls.external_validation: None found: no second cooperative-foraging dataset from another lab.

honest_claim_h3: A model could say which mouse of one of ~40 Mount Sinai pairs will reach the reward zone first from its early movement, in one arena paradigm, but the label is a function of the same trajectories.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use both mice's early movement in a trial to predict which mouse will lead the pair to the reward.
plain_idea.train_on: Nose and neck positions of both mice at 30 frames per second for each trial; 1,024 correct trials verified for one pair, cohort total unknown (40 pairs in the analyses).
plain_idea.predict: Which mouse arrives at the reward zone first (the trial's leader), which the authors compute from the tracked arrival times, not from an independent measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Weak: it would show how early in a trial the role is visible in movement, but the paper already models choices from these features and the answer is mostly in the trajectory itself.

more_or_better_data.why: This is the same data the paper's own MAIRL and logistic models used; the cohort is ~40 pairs from one lab and one arena.

confidence_score.why: No replicate measurement of the label; leader identity is a deterministic function of arrival times.

models_beatable.why: The 2026 MAIRL model was evaluated with within-animal likelihood tests rather than held-out pairs, but the target itself is not a meaningful one to beat.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No accessible new data measuring the same quantity in the same paradigm joins to this one.

ml_idea: Predict trial leader (or reward-zone choice) from the first second of two-mouse trajectories, holding out whole pairs; or decode role from mPFC calcium activity. The first is circular (leader is defined from the trajectories), the second needs the 172 GB imaging archive.

effort.compute_note: Behaviour-only estimate from file sizes; nothing timed. The .mat table may need MATLAB to export, which makes the hours to a feature table unknown.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Try loading ctable_light_combined.mat in Python (h5py/mat73); a MATLAB table object usually comes back as opaque references, which alone stalls the behaviour project.

verdict_reason: The neural data that makes this paper novel is ~172 GB of imaging zips (fails A6), and the behavioural label of interest, which mouse leads, is computed from the same trajectories a model would use (fails A8). On top of that, the only behaviour table is a 785 MB MATLAB table object, with only 40 pairs as independent units.
